record_identity.title: Probabilistic AI-authorship suspicion converted into academic discipline

summary: A Yale student alleges that GPTZero misclassification contributed to a one-year suspension and failing grade after an exam was suspected of AI assistance. Yale disputes his account and says the disciplinary process relied on additional evidence and conduct, leaving the detector’s causal role contested.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Probabilistic AI-authorship scores can acquire institutional authority when embedded in academic discipline even though such detectors have known limitations. The disputed record is useful monitoring evidence but does not yet establish a standalone failure mechanism or Yale liability.

source_records.source_title: How a Yale AI-cheating dispute became a 13-count federal lawsuit
source_records.source_context: Ars documents the student’s allegations, GPTZero’s role, Yale’s additional stated evidence and the continuing federal lawsuit. The parties sharply dispute the meaning and causal significance of the detector result.
source_records.relevance_note: Supports a disputed institutional-authority observation without determining misconduct or liability.

limitations: Yale states the disciplinary record included evidence beyond GPTZero.
The observation does not determine whether misconduct occurred.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to preserve the contested detector-to-discipline pathway and both parties' positions.
